title: Layers basics
summary: Add, rename, paint on and hide a layer.

steps.say: Make sure the Layers panel is showing at the lower right. If it is not, press F7.

check.prompt: Is the Layers panel visible on the right side, listing at least one layer?

hints: F7 shows and hides the panel, so press it again if it disappeared.
Window, then Layers, in the menu bar also opens it.
steps.why: The Layers panel is where you see and control every part of the image.

steps.say: Press Control Shift N to make a new layer, then click OK.

check.prompt: Is there a new layer, such as Layer 1, above the photo in the Layers panel?

hints: Or click the plus button at the bottom of the Layers panel; that skips the dialog.
Layer, then New, then Layer in the menu bar does the same.
steps.why: New strokes go on their own layer so the photo below stays untouched.

steps.say: Double-click the new layer's name and type Sketch, then press Enter.

check.prompt: Is there a layer named Sketch in the Layers panel?

hints: Double-click the name text itself, not the thumbnail, or a settings window opens.
Layer, then Rename Layer in the menu bar works too.
steps.why: Clear names make it quick to find layers later.

steps.say: Press B for the Brush, then paint a few strokes across the photo.

check.prompt: Are there new brush strokes on the image that were not there before?

hints: Press D first to set black as the paint color.
Press the right bracket key to make the brush bigger if strokes are too thin.
steps.why: Painting on the Sketch layer keeps your marks separate from the photo.

steps.say: Click the eye icon to the left of Sketch to hide that layer.

check.prompt: Are the brush strokes now hidden, with the eye icon next to Sketch turned off?

hints: The eye sits in the first column of each row in the Layers panel.
Make sure you click the eye on the Sketch row, not on the photo row.
steps.why: Hiding a layer lets you compare with and without it without deleting anything.

steps.say: Click the same spot again to bring the strokes back.

check.prompt: Are the brush strokes visible again on the photo?

hints: The empty box where the eye was is still clickable.
Control Z also brings back the last change.
steps.why: Layers can be switched on and off as often as you like.
